title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on the Causes of Action for Judicial Compensation Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on Causes of Action for Judicial Compensation Cases

Fa [2023] No. 68

The Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Causes of Action for Judicial Compensation Cases were deliberated and adopted at the 1883rd session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on April 3, 2023, and shall come into force on June 1, 2023. The Provisions on Causes of Action for State Compensation Cases (Fa [2012] No. 32) shall be simultaneously abolished. The Provisions on Causes of Action for Judicial Compensation Cases (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions on Causes of Action") are hereby issued to you, and the following notice is given on matters relating to the application of the Provisions on Causes of Action.

I. Conscientiously Study and Accurately Apply the Provisions on Causes of Action

This revision of the provisions on causes of action adheres to the State Compensation Law as the basis, and focuses on solving problems such as the original provisions being too simplistic and general, the division of causes of action being too rough, and the fact that in the trial practice of judicial compensation, some cases had no applicable cause of action, or the reason for applying for compensation was used to replace the cause of action. The revision of the provisions on causes of action follows the principles of necessity and practicality, respects past usage habits of causes of action, combines the needs of trial practice, and ensures that the revised provisions on causes of action have a complete system, accurate classification, and convenient application.

The accurate application of causes of action in judicial compensation cases is conducive to the refinement of the filing and trial work of the people's courts in judicial compensation, conducive to improving the accuracy of case statistics, and can provide effective reference for the judicial decision-making of the people's courts. People's courts at all levels must fully recognize the importance of accurately applying causes of action in judicial compensation cases, conscientiously study the Provisions on Causes of Action, understand the hierarchical enumeration system and specific application rules of causes of action, accurately select and apply specific causes of action, legally protect the right of claimants to apply for compensation, effectively implement the "people-oriented" concept of judicial compensation trial work in the new era, and continuously promote the refined development of judicial compensation trials.

II. System Arrangement and Determination Criteria for Causes of Action

The Provisions on Causes of Action adhere to the chapter system of the State Compensation Law as the basis, changing the enumeration method of causes of action from the previous flat layout to a hierarchical layout. Based on the two first-level causes of action, "Criminal Compensation" and "Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation," three-level classifications are made so that every judicial compensation case has an applicable cause of action. Among them, the "Criminal Compensation" cause of action is divided into three second-level causes of action according to the object of infringement, namely "Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Personal Liberty," "Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Life and Health," and "Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Property"; the "Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation" cause of action is divided into four second-level causes of action according to the act of infringement, namely "Compensation for Illegally Taking Coercive Measures against Obstruction of Litigation," "Compensation for Illegal Preservation," "Compensation for Illegal Advance Execution," and "Compensation for Erroneous Execution."

The third-level causes of action are based on the original 14 causes of action. Except for "Compensation for Illegal Preservation" and "Compensation for Erroneous Execution," which are retained as second-level causes of action, the other 12 original causes of action are retained as third-level causes of action. At the same time, according to the needs of judicial compensation trial practice, 8 new third-level causes of action are added, namely "Compensation for De Facto Custody," "Compensation for Injury or Death Due to Neglect of Supervisory Duties," "Compensation for Illegal Confiscation or Unjustified Refusal to Return Bail Deposits," and the causes of action for judicial compensation related to execution: "Compensation for Execution Without Basis or Beyond Scope," "Compensation for Illegal Execution Damaging the Rights and Interests of Third Parties," "Compensation for Illegally Taking Execution Measures," "Compensation for Illegally Taking Coercive Execution Measures," and "Compensation for Illegal Non-Execution or Delay in Execution."

III. Specific Application Rules for Causes of Action

(A) General Application Rules

The Provisions on Causes of Action achieve full coverage of all types of judicial compensation cases in the people's courts. When applying specifically, no other causes of action should be created beyond those provided in the Provisions on Causes of Action, such as "Other Compensation" or "State Compensation." The application should follow the principle of hierarchy from bottom to top: first apply the third-level cause of action; if there is no corresponding third-level cause of action, apply the second-level cause of action; if the second-level cause of action still does not correspond, apply the first-level cause of action. Where a lower-level cause of action is applicable, the next higher-level cause of action cannot be applied directly. For example, if a claimant claims compensation for infringement of personal liberty due to illegal criminal detention by the compensation obligor, the applicable third-level cause of action is "Compensation for Illegal Criminal Detention," not "Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Personal Liberty" or "Criminal Compensation."

(B) Application Rules for Alternative Causes of Action

In this revision, there are 9 alternative causes of action in the Provisions on Causes of Action, namely: "Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Extraction of Confessions by Torture," "Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Assault or Abuse," "Compensation for Injury or Death Due to Neglect of Supervisory Duties," "Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Illegal Use of Weapons or Police Equipment," "Compensation for Criminal Illegal Sealing, Seizing, Freezing, or Confiscation," "Compensation for Illegal Confiscation or Unjustified Refusal to Return Bail Deposits," "Compensation for Erroneous Imposition of Fines or Confiscation of Property," "Compensation for Execution Without Basis or Beyond Scope," and "Compensation for Illegal Non-Execution or Delay in Execution." When applying alternative causes of action, the determination shall be made based on the specific reasons and claims of the claimant. For example, if a claimant claims compensation for physical disability caused by extraction of confessions by torture by the compensation obligor, the cause of action should be "Compensation for Injury Caused by Extraction of Confessions by Torture," not "Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Extraction of Confessions by Torture"; if a claimant claims compensation for property loss caused by illegal seizure or confiscation of property by the compensation obligor during criminal proceedings, the cause of action should be "Compensation for Criminal Illegal Seizure or Confiscation," not "Compensation for Criminal Illegal Sealing, Seizing, Freezing, or Confiscation."

(C) Rules for Combined Application of Multiple Causes of Action

Where the compensation obligor has committed multiple infringing acts and the claimant claims compensation for all of them in a single case, different causes of action may be applied in parallel. For example, if a claimant claims compensation for illegal criminal detention and extraction of confessions by torture causing physical injury, the cause of action should be "Compensation for Illegal Criminal Detention and Injury Caused by Extraction of Confessions by Torture." If multiple causes of action belong to different levels, the causes of action shall be arranged in ascending order. For example, if a claimant claims that the executing court erroneously executed property over which the claimant had a right of pledge, and during the appeal process there were acts of pulling and dragging causing physical injury, the third-level cause of action "Compensation for Illegal Execution Damaging the Rights and Interests of Third Parties" and the first-level cause of action "Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation" may be applied, and in the decision document it may be expressed as "Illegal Execution Damaging the Rights and Interests of Third Parties, Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation."

IV. Other Issues to Note

(A) People's courts at all levels must accurately grasp the nature and function of causes of action in judicial compensation cases. The Provisions on Causes of Action are not provisions on the scope of accepting judicial compensation cases. When determining whether a specific case falls within the scope of accepting cases, the people's court shall make a judgment based on the State Compensation Law and relevant judicial interpretations, and shall not use the Provisions on Causes of Action as the basis for such judgment.

(B) Where the matter for which compensation is claimed does not fall within the adjustment scope of the State Compensation Law, the people's court may determine the corresponding cause of action based on the specific reasons for the compensation claim. For example, if a claimant was acquitted in a retrial before the implementation of the State Compensation Law and applies for state compensation, although it does not fall within the scope of accepting state compensation cases of the people's court, the cause of action "Compensation for Acquittal in Retrial" may still be applied. If compensation is sought from the people's court that made the original erroneous judgment on the grounds of erroneous civil or administrative judgments, the cause of action "Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation" may be applied.

(C) The expression of the case name shall be consistent with the expression of the cause of action, and the reason for applying for compensation shall not replace the cause of action. For example, if a claimant claims compensation for infringement of property rights due to illegal preservation by a people's court, the case name shall be expressed as "So-and-so's Application for Compensation for Illegal Preservation by the XX People's Court," and shall not be expressed as "So-and-so's Application for State Compensation from the XX People's Court on the Grounds of Illegal Preservation."

(D) After this notice is issued, higher people's courts at all levels shall effectively organize the study and training of the Provisions on Causes of Action for relevant personnel within their jurisdiction, ensuring that training reaches all personnel, especially those engaged in case filing registration and judicial statistics. In the future, when filling in the cause of action using the Provisions on Causes of Action, people's courts at all levels must earnestly assume responsibility and fill it in carefully in accordance with the requirements of this notice. The Supreme People's Court will, from time to time, issue criticism notices for courts that fail to conduct training or are irresponsible and fill in causes of action arbitrarily.

April 19, 2023

Provisions on Causes of Action for Judicial Compensation Cases

(Adopted at the 1883rd session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on April 3, 2023, and effective as of June 1, 2023)

For the purpose of correctly applying the law and uniformly determining causes of action, in accordance with the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China and other legal provisions, and taking into account the actual circumstances of the judicial compensation trial work of the people's courts, the causes of action for judicial compensation cases are hereby provided as follows:

I. Criminal Compensation

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, in the exercise of criminal judicial powers, infringed upon personal rights or property rights.

(A) Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Personal Liberty

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, in the exercise of criminal judicial powers, infringed upon personal liberty.

1. Compensation for Illegal Criminal Detention

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor took detention measures in violation of the conditions, procedures, or time limits provided for in the Criminal Procedure Law.

2. Compensation for De Facto Custody

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, in violation of the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, imposed residential surveillance at a designated location or conducted continuous summons or custodial summons beyond the statutory time limit, which actually achieved the effect of criminal detention.

3. Compensation for Wrongful Arrest

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor took arrest measures erroneously.

4. Compensation for Acquittal on Appeal

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the second instance has changed the conviction to acquittal, and the compensation obligor previously made an erroneous first-instance guilty judgment.

5. Compensation for Acquittal on Retrial

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that after the second instance remanded the case for retrial, the case was treated as not guilty, and the compensation obligor previously made an erroneous first-instance guilty judgment.

6. Compensation for Acquittal in Retrial

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that, in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the retrial has changed the conviction to acquittal or partial acquittal, and the compensation obligor previously made the original effective erroneous guilty judgment.

(B) Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Life and Health

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, in the exercise of criminal judicial powers, infringed upon life and health.

1. Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Extraction of Confessions by Torture

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor extracted confessions by torture, causing physical injury or death.

2. Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Assault or Abuse

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor committed acts of assault or abuse, or instigated or allowed others to commit acts of assault or abuse, causing physical injury or death.

3. Compensation for Injury or Death Due to Neglect of Supervisory Duties

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor failed to fulfill its statutory supervisory and treatment duties, causing physical injury or death to a person in custody.

4. Compensation for Injury or Death Caused by Illegal Use of Weapons or Police Equipment

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor illegally used weapons or police equipment, causing physical injury or death.

(C) Criminal Compensation for Infringement of Property

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, in the exercise of criminal judicial powers, infringed upon property rights.

1. Compensation for Criminal Illegal Sealing, Seizing, Freezing, or Confiscation

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor, during criminal proceedings, illegally took measures of sealing, seizing, freezing, or confiscating property.

2. Compensation for Illegal Confiscation or Unjustified Refusal to Return Bail Deposits

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that the compensation obligor illegally confiscated a bail deposit, or without justifiable reasons refused to return a bail deposit that should have been returned.

3. Compensation for Erroneous Imposition of Fines or Confiscation of Property

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that after the original judgment of a fine or confiscation of property was executed, the property-related punishment has been changed in a retrial conducted in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.

II. Non-Criminal Judicial Compensation

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil, administrative, or other non-criminal judicial activities, infringed upon personal rights or property rights.

(D) Compensation for Illegally Taking Coercive Measures against Obstruction of Litigation

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil or administrative proceedings, illegally took coercive measures against obstruction of litigation.

1. Compensation for Illegal Judicial Fines

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil or administrative proceedings, illegally imposed a judicial fine.

2. Compensation for Illegal Judicial Detention

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil or administrative proceedings, illegally imposed judicial detention.

(E) Compensation for Illegal Preservation

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil or administrative proceedings, illegally took or illegally lifted preservation measures.

(F) Compensation for Illegal Advance Execution

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court, in civil or administrative proceedings, illegally took advance execution measures.

(G) Compensation for Erroneous Execution

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court erroneously executed civil or administrative judgments, rulings, or other effective legal instruments.

1. Compensation for Execution Without Basis or Beyond Scope

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court executed a legal instrument that was not yet effective, or executed beyond the amount or scope determined in the effective legal instrument.

2. Compensation for Illegal Execution Damaging the Rights and Interests of Third Parties

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court illegally executed property of a third party, failed to protect the third party's legal rights and interests such as priority rights, or illegally executed property that had already been legally preserved or executed by another court.

3. Compensation for Illegally Taking Execution Measures

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court illegally took execution measures such as sealing, seizing, freezing, auctioning, selling, satisfying debts with property, or delivery, or committed faults such as failing to fulfill supervisory duties in the process of taking such measures.

4. Compensation for Illegally Taking Coercive Execution Measures

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court illegally took coercive execution measures such as inclusion on the list of dishonest judgment debtors, restriction of consumption, restriction of exit, fines, or detention.

5. Compensation for Illegal Non-Execution or Delay in Execution

Applicable to compensation cases in which the claimant claims that a people's court illegally failed to execute, delayed execution, or failed to resume execution as required by law when it should have.
